_comment: Closed variety (FR-13): the usual test names. It is a SUGGESTION and a FALLBACK, never a refusal or a permission (D-0030, 06.10.2026): onboarding proposes candidate test locations by these names (scripts/test_locations.py --suggest), and scripts/test_locations.py is_test_path falls back to them to recognise a test when the project named none of its own. A project that names its tests another way gets its own entry in `test_locations` in qa-factory/config.json (the person's word), not a refusal and not an entry in this file. All lower-case. A path carries a usual test name when (a) a FOLDER segment equals a dir_names entry or ends with a dir_suffixes entry (with at least one character before it), or (b) the LAST segment's stem (without its final extension) starts with a stem_prefixes entry or ends with a stem_suffixes entry, the marker's characters literal. `skip_dirs` (optional) are folder names the suggest/check walk never enters (dependencies, build output); absent means none. The list was first written as the branch author's word of 03.10.2026 (D-0025). `stem_camel_suffixes` (case-sensitive, unlike the other lists) names the CamelCase endings of a test class file (FooTests.cs, FooTest.java, FooSpec.scala): the stem ends with one, with at least one character before it, and an all-upper-case ending (IT) is not preceded by an upper-case letter (so AUDIT.java is no test); `code_extensions` (lower-case, with the dot) says which files are code at all; `test-harness` in `dir_names` keeps the historical exclusion of that folder from the production count;`classic` (B-407 A, FR-13; G1-1) holds the `folders` (as written, case-exact) that are a test place BY THEMSELVES for the production question: a file under one of them is a test; a usual name (any list above) needs a usual folder beside it, or a place the project's config names (`roots.test`, `tests_root`, `run.levels`), and a name ALONE never drops a production file (`scripts/test_files.py` and `src/app/test_mode.py` are application code, a colocated `a.test.ts` stays production); `prefixes` and `suffixes` no longer decide anything there and stay until G2-1 decides on them; an absent or malformed `classic` is read as the built-in floor in scripts/test_files.py; `fence_languages` (extension, lower-case with the dot, to the word that opens a markdown code fence) is read by scripts/repo_map.py through `test_files.fence_language`: an extension with no entry gets a bare fence.
